system.overview: The Washington Metro, operated by WMATA, is the rapid transit system serving the Washington metropolitan area. It is the second-busiest rapid transit system in the United States and serves the District of Columbia, along with portions of Maryland and Virginia.

history.title: System Opens
history.description: Metro opens with the first segment of the Red Line between Rhode Island Avenue and Farragut North, comprising 4.6 miles and 5 stations.

history.title: Blue Line Opens
history.description: Blue Line service begins between National Airport and Stadium-Armory.

history.title: Orange Line Opens
history.description: Orange Line begins service between New Carrollton and Ballston.

history.title: Green Line Opens
history.description: Green Line opens between U Street and Anacostia.

history.title: System Completed
history.description: The original 103-mile Adopted Regional System is completed with the opening of the Green Line to Branch Avenue.

history.title: Silver Line Phase 1
history.description: Silver Line Phase 1 opens, extending service to Tysons Corner and Reston.

history.title: Silver Line Phase 2
history.description: Silver Line Phase 2 opens, extending service to Dulles International Airport and Loudoun County.

red.name: Red Line
red.description: The Red Line is the oldest and busiest line in the Metrorail system, connecting Shady Grove in Montgomery County, Maryland to Glenmont via downtown Washington, D.C.

blue.name: Blue Line
blue.description: The Blue Line serves Fairfax County, Arlington County, and Prince George's County, passing through downtown D.C. and connecting to Reagan National Airport.

orange.name: Orange Line
orange.description: The Orange Line connects Fairfax County, Virginia to Prince George's County, Maryland, serving Vienna, Falls Church, Arlington, and downtown D.C.

green.name: Green Line
green.description: The Green Line runs from Greenbelt in Prince George's County to Branch Avenue, serving the U Street corridor and Anacostia neighborhoods.

yellow.name: Yellow Line
yellow.description: The Yellow Line is the shortest line in the system, connecting Huntington in Fairfax County to Mt Vernon Square in D.C., serving Pentagon and Reagan National Airport.

silver.name: Silver Line
silver.description: The Silver Line is the newest line in the system, connecting Loudoun County and Dulles International Airport to downtown D.C. and Prince George's County.

metro-center.description: Metro Center is the central hub of the Metrorail system, located at the intersection of G Street and 12th/13th Streets NW. It is one of the busiest stations in the system and serves as a transfer point between the Red, Blue, Orange, and Silver lines.

gallery-place.description: Gallery Place-Chinatown serves the Penn Quarter and Chinatown neighborhoods. The station is adjacent to Capital One Arena and the National Portrait Gallery.

union-station.description: Union Station serves the historic Union Station, providing connections to Amtrak, MARC, and VRE commuter rail services, as well as intercity bus services.

pentagon.description: Pentagon station serves the United States Department of Defense headquarters. It is one of the deepest stations in the system at 97 feet below ground.

reagan-national-airport.description: This station provides direct access to Reagan National Airport, serving as a major transportation hub for air travelers to the Washington area.

dulles-airport.description: The newest major station on the Silver Line, providing direct rail access to Dulles International Airport for the first time.

farragut-north.description: Located in the central business district, Farragut North is one of the original five stations that opened with the system in 1976.

farragut-west.description: Farragut West serves the western portion of downtown D.C. and is located near the White House and World Bank headquarters.

shady-grove.description: Shady Grove is the northwestern terminus of the Red Line, located in Montgomery County, Maryland with extensive parking facilities.

glenmont.description: Glenmont is the northeastern terminus of the Red Line and was the final Red Line station to open.

l-enfant-plaza.description: L'Enfant Plaza is one of the most important transfer stations in the system, serving all lines except the Red Line. It is adjacent to the Smithsonian museums.

rosslyn.description: Rosslyn is the deepest station in the system at 97 feet below ground and serves as the gateway between D.C. and Northern Virginia.

bethesda.description: Bethesda station serves the downtown Bethesda business district in Montgomery County, Maryland.

silver-spring.description: Silver Spring is a major transit hub providing connections to MARC commuter rail and numerous bus routes.

tysons-corner.description: Tysons Corner station serves the major commercial center and shopping destination in Fairfax County, Virginia.

ashburn.description: Ashburn is the western terminus of the Silver Line, serving Loudoun County's rapidly growing data center corridor.

navy-yard.description: Navy Yard-Ballpark serves the Capitol Riverfront neighborhood and Nationals Park, home of the Washington Nationals.

u-street.description: U Street serves the historic U Street Corridor, known for its jazz heritage and nightlife, and is near the African American Civil War Memorial.

columbia-heights.description: Columbia Heights station serves the Columbia Heights neighborhood and the DC USA shopping center.

vienna.description: Vienna is the western terminus of the Orange Line, serving Fairfax County and George Mason University.

dupont-circle.description: Dupont Circle serves the vibrant Dupont Circle neighborhood, known for its embassies, restaurants, and LGBTQ+ community.

woodley-park.description: Serves the Woodley Park neighborhood and provides access to the Smithsonian National Zoo.

cleveland-park.description: Cleveland Park station serves a residential neighborhood with historic homes and local shops.

van-ness-udc.description: Serves the Van Ness neighborhood and the University of the District of Columbia.

tenleytown-au.description: Serves American University and the Tenleytown commercial district.

friendship-heights.description: Located on the D.C./Maryland border, serving a major retail district.

medical-center.description: Serves the National Institutes of Health and Walter Reed National Military Medical Center.

grosvenor-strathmore.description: Serves the Strathmore music center and surrounding residential areas.

white-flint.description: Serves the Pike District redevelopment area in North Bethesda.

twinbrook.description: Serves the Twinbrook neighborhood and nearby commercial areas in Rockville.

rockville.description: Serves downtown Rockville with connections to MARC Brunswick Line commuter rail.

wheaton.description: Features one of the longest single-span escalators in the Western Hemisphere at 230 feet.

forest-glen.description: The deepest station in the system at 196 feet below ground, with no escalators—only elevators.

takoma.description: Serves the Takoma neighborhood near the D.C./Maryland border.

brookland-cua.description: Serves Catholic University of America and the Brookland neighborhood.

rhode-island-ave.address: 919 Rhode Island Ave NE, Washington, DC 20018
rhode-island-ave.description: One of the original five stations, serving the Brentwood and Woodridge neighborhoods.

noma-gallaudet.description: Serves the NoMa business district and Gallaudet University, the only university for the deaf and hard of hearing.

judiciary-square.description: Serves the D.C. courts, city offices, and the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial.

mcpherson-square.description: Located in the central business district, serving K Street and nearby office buildings.

federal-triangle.description: Serves the Federal Triangle complex of government buildings including the IRS and EPA headquarters.

smithsonian.description: Central access point for the National Mall and Smithsonian museums.

federal-center-sw.description: Serves federal office buildings and the U.S. Botanic Garden.

capitol-south.description: Primary station for the U.S. Capitol and House office buildings.

eastern-market.description: Serves the Capitol Hill neighborhood and the historic Eastern Market.

potomac-ave.description: Serves the Hill East neighborhood near the Anacostia River.

stadium-armory.description: Serves the D.C. Armory and formerly served RFK Stadium. Major transfer point to Blue Line.

benning-road.description: Serves the Benning neighborhood in Northeast D.C.

capitol-heights.description: First station in Prince George's County on the Blue Line.

addison-road.description: Serves the Seat Pleasant community with large park-and-ride facilities.

morgan-boulevard.description: Serves FedEx Field, home of the Washington Commanders.

largo-town-center.description: Eastern terminus of the Blue and Silver Lines, serving Prince George's County.

minnesota-ave.description: Serves the Minnesota Avenue corridor in Northeast D.C.

deanwood.description: Serves the Deanwood neighborhood in Northeast D.C.

cheverly.address: 5701 Columbia Park Rd, Landover Hills, MD 20784
cheverly.description: First station in Prince George's County on the Orange Line.

landover.description: Serves the Landover area with major park-and-ride facilities.

new-carrollton.address: 4700 Garden City Dr, New Carrollton, MD 20784
new-carrollton.description: Eastern terminus of the Orange Line with Amtrak and MARC connections.

court-house.description: Serves the Arlington County courthouse and government complex.

clarendon.description: Serves the Clarendon neighborhood, known for restaurants and nightlife.

virginia-square.description: Serves George Mason University's Arlington campus and Virginia Square.

ballston-mu.description: Serves the Ballston commercial district and Marymount University.

east-falls-church.address: 2001 N Sycamore St, Falls Church, VA 22043
east-falls-church.description: Where Orange and Silver lines split; serves Falls Church area.

west-falls-church.description: Serves the West Falls Church area with major bus connections.

dunn-loring.description: Serves the Merrifield area and Mosaic District.

crystal-city.description: Serves the Crystal City business district with connection to VRE commuter rail.

pentagon-city.description: Serves Pentagon City mall and the surrounding residential area.

braddock-road.description: Serves the Braddock Road neighborhood in Alexandria.

king-street.description: Major transit hub serving Old Town Alexandria with Amtrak and VRE connections.

eisenhower-ave.description: Serves the Eisenhower Valley commercial area.

huntington.description: Southern terminus of the Yellow Line with large parking facilities.

van-dorn-street.description: Serves the west Alexandria/Van Dorn area.

franconia-springfield.description: Southern terminus of the Blue Line with Amtrak, VRE, and extensive bus connections.

archives.description: Serves the National Archives, Navy Memorial, and Penn Quarter entertainment district.

mt-vernon-sq.description: Serves the Walter E. Washington Convention Center and historic Shaw neighborhood.

shaw-howard.description: Serves the Shaw neighborhood and Howard University.

georgia-ave-petworth.description: Serves the Petworth neighborhood and Georgia Avenue corridor.

fort-totten.description: Major transfer point between Red and Green/Yellow lines.

west-hyattsville.description: Serves Hyattsville and the University of Maryland area.

prince-georges-plaza.description: Serves the Prince George's Plaza retail area.

college-park.description: Serves the University of Maryland with MARC Camden Line connection.

greenbelt.description: Northern terminus of the Green Line with MARC and extensive bus connections.

waterfront.description: Serves the Southwest Waterfront and The Wharf development.

anacostia.description: Serves the historic Anacostia neighborhood east of the Anacostia River.

congress-heights.description: Serves the Congress Heights neighborhood and St. Elizabeths campus.

southern-avenue.description: Located on the D.C./Maryland border at Southern Avenue.

naylor-road.description: Serves the Naylor Road area in Prince George's County.

suitland.description: Serves Suitland and the Census Bureau headquarters.

branch-ave.description: Southern terminus of the Green Line with extensive parking.

reston-town-center.description: Serves Reston Town Center's urban core and surrounding businesses.

herndon.description: Serves the Town of Herndon and surrounding residential areas.

innovation-center.description: Serves Fairfax County's Innovation Center area and data center corridor.

loudoun-gateway.description: First station in Loudoun County, serving the Route 606 corridor.

mclean.description: Serves downtown McLean and Capital One headquarters.

spring-hill.description: Serves the Spring Hill area of Tysons.

greensboro.description: Serves Tysons Galleria and surrounding office buildings.

wiehle-reston-east.description: Major park-and-ride station serving Reston with 2,300 parking spaces.

foggy-bottom.description: Serves George Washington University, the State Department, and Kennedy Center.

arlington-cemetery.description: Serves Arlington National Cemetery. No parking available; no Sunday service on Blue Line.

railcars.name: 1000 Series
railcars.description: The 1000 Series was the original fleet of Metrorail cars that opened with the system in 1976. These cars featured carpeted floors and cushioned seats, which were unique among American transit systems at the time. They were completely retired by 2017.

railcars.name: 2000 Series
railcars.description: The 2000 Series were purchased to expand the fleet for the extension of the Orange Line. They were similar in design to the 1000 Series and were the first cars built by Breda for WMATA.

railcars.name: 3000 Series
railcars.description: The 3000 Series continued the expansion of the Metrorail fleet and introduced minor improvements over earlier series. These cars served until 2019 and were among the last pre-rehabilitation cars.

railcars.name: 4000 Series
railcars.description: The 4000 Series were the first Metrorail cars to use AC propulsion systems. Only 100 were built as WMATA moved toward rehabilitating existing cars.

railcars.name: 5000 Series
railcars.description: The 5000 Series represented a significant upgrade with modern electronics and improved reliability. They feature fabric-covered seats and improved lighting.

railcars.name: 6000 Series
railcars.description: The 6000 Series continued the modernization of the fleet with improved passenger amenities and environmental controls. They are currently in active service.

railcars.name: 7000 Series
railcars.description: The 7000 Series is the newest generation of Metrorail cars, featuring digital displays, LED lighting, and improved accessibility. They are designed to eventually replace all older railcar series and are the largest single order in WMATA history.
